scenarios.title: Repair diagnostics that hide a failed investigation
scenarios.summary: Add useful trace output while retaining the investigation’s stdout, error status and input files.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly MODE FILE, with MODE quiet or trace; otherwise print Usage: inspect quiet-or-trace FILE on stderr and exit2 before any trace. FILE must be a one-line ASCII name matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$; invalid names print Invalid file on stderr and exit2 before tracing. For a valid interface, trace mode writes Trace: reading FILE on stderr first. quiet mode writes no trace lines. A missing input prints Missing file: FILE on stderr, no stdout, and finishes with status2. For an existing input, select literal ERROR lines in original order. With matches, print Findings: then each complete matching line on stdout and finish with status0. With none, print No findings on stdout and finish with status1. Output lines end with LF; preserve spaces/backslashes within matched text. Trace mode writes Trace: result N on stderr last, using the actual final investigation status. Diagnostics must not change that status or contaminate stdout. Keep every virtual file unchanged.
steps: Repair and test the full script

initial.source:
usage() { printf 'Usage: inspect quiet-or-trace FILE\n' >&2; exit 2; }
if test "$#" -ne 2; then usage; fi
mode=$1
file=$2
case "$mode" in quiet|trace) : ;; *) usage ;; esac
case "$file" in *'
'*) printf 'Invalid file\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
if printf '%s\n' "$file" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$'; then :; else printf 'Invalid file\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test "$mode" = trace; then printf 'Trace: reading %s\n' "$file"; fi
if test -f "$file"; then
  matches=$(grep -F 'ERROR' "$file")
  printf 'Filter finished\n'
  result=$?
  if test "$result" -eq 0; then
    printf 'Findings:\n%s\n'  $matches
  else
    printf 'No findings\n'
  fi
else
  printf 'Missing file: %s\n' "$file" >&2
  result=2
fi
if test "$mode" = trace; then printf 'Trace: result %s\n' "$result" >&2; fi
exit "$result"

concepts.title: A script has separate results
concepts.text: Standard output is the business report; standard error is where this task places diagnostics. Exit status is a third result: 0 means findings, 1 means none, and 2 means the specified input error. A trace message must not quietly change one of those results.

concepts.title: Save status before reporting
concepts.text: $? belongs to the most recently finished command. A successful printf changes it to 0. Immediately save a meaningful status with result=$?; use that saved variable for later messages and exit. The worked example deliberately starts with false, whose status is 1.

concepts.title: Add tracing deliberately
concepts.text: The assignment uses its own quiet/trace argument, not Bash set -x. Gate Trace lines on that argument and send them with >&2. Quote captured matches when printing so spaces and literal wildcard text stay intact. This is manual instrumentation within the supported subset.

teaching.example:
false
result=$?
printf 'Trace: saved result %s\n' "$result" >&2
printf 'Business report stays on stdout\n'
exit "$result"

scenarios.title: Resume a checked handover without trusting its checkpoint
scenarios.summary: Reconcile saved work with its actual outputs, validate the whole request, then preview or finish only pending work.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly preview or apply as one argument; otherwise print Usage: resume preview-or-apply on stderr and exit2. Then require jobs.txt and checkpoint.txt in that order; a missing file prints Missing file: NAME on stderr and exits2. jobs.txt contains 0–8 LF-separated IDs; a final LF is optional. Every ID must match ASCII ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,5}$ and be unique. Blank/invalid/duplicate/excess rows print Invalid jobs on stderr and exit2. Then every checkpoint.txt row must be a unique requested ID, or print Invalid checkpoint and exit2. Validate outputs in jobs order before printing a plan or changing any file. A checkpointed ID needs ID.done containing exactly Completed: ID plus one LF; otherwise print Checkpoint mismatch: ID and exit2. A non-checkpointed ID must have no ID.done file; if present print Untracked output: ID and exit2. The first such problem wins. On successful validation, stdout lists Already: ID or Pending: ID for each job in jobs order, then Already count: N and Pending count: N. All lines end with LF; success has empty stderr and status0. preview changes no files. apply writes Completed: ID plus one LF to each pending ID.done, retains all existing completed outputs, and writes checkpoint.txt as every job ID in jobs order with LF after each (empty for no jobs). Preserve jobs.txt and every unrelated file. Any specified error has no stdout and leaves every file unchanged. This is deterministic reconciliation of supplied prior work, not real crash recovery, atomic publication, locks or concurrent execution.

initial.source:
# This attempt writes too soon and trusts substring matches. Repair it.
mode=$1
already=0
pending=0
while IFS= read -r id || test -n "$id"; do
  if grep -F "$id" checkpoint.txt; then
    already=$((already+1))
  else
    printf 'Completed: %s\n' "$id" > "$id.done"
    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> checkpoint.txt
    pending=$((pending+1))
  fi
done < jobs.txt
printf 'Already count: %s\nPending count: %s\n' "$already" "$pending"

solution:
if test "$#" -ne 1; then printf 'Usage: resume preview-or-apply\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
mode=$1
case "$mode" in preview|apply) : ;; *) printf 'Usage: resume preview-or-apply\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
for file in jobs.txt checkpoint.txt; do
  if test -f "$file"; then :; else printf 'Missing file: %s\n' "$file" >&2; exit 2; fi
done
jobs=()
seen='|'
while IFS= read -r id || test -n "$id"; do
  if printf '%s\n' "$id" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,5}$'; then :; else printf 'Invalid jobs\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
  case "$seen" in *"|$id|"*) printf 'Invalid jobs\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  seen=$seen$id'|'
  jobs=( "${jobs[@]}" "$id" )
  if test "${#jobs[@]}" -gt 8; then printf 'Invalid jobs\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
done < jobs.txt
completed='|'
while IFS= read -r id || test -n "$id"; do
  case "$seen" in *"|$id|"*) : ;; *) printf 'Invalid checkpoint\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  case "$completed" in *"|$id|"*) printf 'Invalid checkpoint\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  completed=$completed$id'|'
done < checkpoint.txt
pending=()
already=0
ledger=''
plan=''
for id in "${jobs[@]}"; do
  case "$completed" in
    *"|$id|"*)
      if test -f "$id.done"; then :; else printf 'Checkpoint mismatch: %s\n' "$id" >&2; exit 2; fi
      actual=$(cat "$id.done"; printf '.')
      expected='Completed: '$id'
.'
      if test "$actual" = "$expected"; then :; else printf 'Checkpoint mismatch: %s\n' "$id" >&2; exit 2; fi
      plan=$plan'Already: '$id'
'
      already=$((already+1))
      ;;
    *)
      if test -f "$id.done"; then printf 'Untracked output: %s\n' "$id" >&2; exit 2; fi
      pending=( "${pending[@]}" "$id" )
      plan=$plan'Pending: '$id'
'
      ;;
  esac
  ledger=$ledger$id'
'
done
if test "$mode" = apply; then
  for id in "${pending[@]}"; do printf 'Completed: %s\n' "$id" > "$id.done"; done
  printf '%s' "$ledger" > checkpoint.txt
fi
printf '%sAlready count: %s\nPending count: %s\n' "$plan" "$already" "${#pending[@]}"
exit 0

concepts.title: A checkpoint is a claim, not proof
concepts.text: A saved list says which jobs were finished earlier. Before skipping them, compare that claim with their actual output. A missing or changed completed output is a reconciliation error; silently overwriting it would hide the inconsistency.

concepts.title: Validate the whole request before writing
concepts.text: Collect and validate every job and checkpoint first. Then inspect all requested outputs. An error near the end must leave earlier pending jobs untouched. Bash arrays can hold pending IDs until this preflight is complete; quoted "${pending[@]}" keeps each ID a separate item.

concepts.title: Separate observation from repair
concepts.text: The worked example only observes whether two different sample outputs exist. The assignment requires stronger evidence: exact contents and validated checkpoint membership. preview reports decisions without writes; apply uses the same validated plan to finish pending work.

concepts.title: Compare exact text and keep recovery honest
concepts.text: Command substitution removes final LFs. To check exact output, append a non-LF sentinel inside the capture and compare against expected text with the same sentinel. This technique was taught in snapshot comparison. Runs start with supplied simulated prior work; no interrupted execution is being resumed.
